proposals.after: Staff filled out with Yin Xiang and Pang Yan as chief clerks, Yao Huang and Yin Wei as marshals, a corps of Tianshui aides—Di Bozhi, Jiao Qian, Liang Xi, Pang Wei, Ren Qian—scribes Jiang Xun and Yan Zun, advisers Wang Ju, Jiao Shi, Jiang Xiu, Yin Yannian, Niu Shuang, and Zhang Qian, and column leaders Wang Qinlu, Yao Fangcheng, Wang Polu, Yang Nan, Yin Song, Pei Qi, Zhao Yao, Di Guang, Dang Shan and others.

proposals.after: When wanderers under Guo Yi seized Tangyi's interior minister Liu Shi and handed him to Xiang, the court reeled and named Zhou Min of the personnel ministry general of the central army to brace the Yangzi.

proposals.after: More than a thousand displaced persons led by Guo Yi seized Jin's interior administrator of Tangyi, Liu Shi, and surrendered him to Xiang; the court trembled greatly and appointed Minister of Personnel Zhou Min central army general to guard the river line.

proposals.after: Shi Zhi's coup brought Xiang credentials as General of Agile Cavalry, Wuhuan colonel, Yuzhou inspector, and duke of Xinchang.

proposals.after: When Shi Zhi assumed title he appointed Xiang credential-bearing inspector, General of Agile Cavalry, Colonel of the Wuhuan, Inspector of Yuzhou, and Duke of Xinchang.

proposals.before: Yi replied, "You assumed Yao would bully neighbors with arms, so he trained men to restore order—the horse thieves were guarding themselves."
proposals.after: Yi replied, "You took Yao the northern pacifier for a man who strengthens himself by force and cannot finally be kept; you drill troops intending to punish disloyalty—those who took horses sought only to defend themselves."
proposals.reason: Quan Yi is explaining Yin Hao's hostility: Hao thought Yao dangerous and drilled troops to punish disloyalty; horse-taking was self-defense against Hao. Both fields make Yao (or an ambiguous 'he') the drillmaster and distort 將懲不恪 / 以威武自強.

proposals.after: Yi said: "The general supposed Lord Yao the northern pacifier relied on martial force and would ultimately be hard to keep; you drill and train troops, about to punish those who are not dutiful; those who took horses sought only self-defense."
proposals.reason: Quan Yi is explaining Yin Hao's hostility: Hao thought Yao dangerous and drilled troops to punish disloyalty; horse-taking was self-defense against Hao. Both fields make Yao (or an ambiguous 'he') the drillmaster and distort 將懲不恪 / 以威武自強.

proposals.before: His staff took shape with Wang Liang of Taiyuan as chief clerk, Yin Chi of Tianshui as marshal, Fu Zicheng and Heina of Lüeyang flanking the van and wings, Lian Qi of Nan'an on the right, Qiang Bai covering the rear, and Xue Zan with Quan Yi as advisers.

proposals.reason: Idiomatic collapses distinct posts: Fu Zicheng is left-wing commander and Heina is van commander; they are not a shared 'flanking the van and wings' pair. Also drops Taiyuan/Lüeyang on the two advisers. Literal is propositionally complete.

proposals.before: The Jin court answered with credentials naming him general who pacifies the north, Bingzhou inspector, and duke of Jiuqiu county.
proposals.after: The Jin court answered with credentials naming him general who pacifies the north, Bingzhou inspector, and duke of Jiqiu county.

proposals.before: The snub deepened Hao's spite: he planted Liu Qi on Qiao, shunted Xiang to Lihao terrace in Liang commandery, and tabled him as interior minister there.
proposals.after: The snub deepened Hao's spite: he planted Liu Qi on Qiao, shunted Xiang to Li Terrace in Liang commandery, and tabled him as interior minister there.
proposals.reason: 蠡台 is Li Terrace / Litai (蠡 lí + 台). 'Lihao' invents a syllable; ZZTJ parallel in-repo uses Li Terrace.

proposals.before: Hao hated him the more and therefore sent General Liu Qi to hold Qiao, moved Xiang to Lihao Terrace in Liang state, and memorialized appointment as administrator of Liang state.
proposals.after: Hao hated him the more and therefore sent General Liu Qi to hold Qiao, moved Xiang to Li Terrace in Liang state, and memorialized appointment as administrator of Liang state.

proposals.before: He barked, "Tell me—does this old Qiang still look fit to crush dogs?"
proposals.after: He barked, "Tell me—does this old Qiang still look fit to crush rebels?"
proposals.reason: 破賊 is break/crush rebels (or bandits), not dogs. Idiomatic invents 'dogs'; literal is fine.

proposals.before: While they were boys you surrounded them with rogues instead of steady ministers—look how they cut each other down.
proposals.after: While they were boys you failed to set good men beside them as ministers—look how they cut each other down.
proposals.reason: Chinese states failure to appoint good assistants (不能使好人輔相), not active stocking of rogues. Idiomatic invents a positive bad appointment.

proposals.before: His chief clerk Wang Liang remonstrated with Xiang: "Your lordship's strategy overshadows the realm; soldiers long to spend their lives for you—you cannot waste prestige and tire the host guarding this lone city.
proposals.after: His chief clerk Wang Liang remonstrated with Xiang: "Your lordship's strategy overshadows the realm; soldiers long to spend their lives for you—you cannot waste prestige and tire the host by clinging to this lone city.
proposals.reason: In the Luoyang siege context, 守此孤城 means lingering on / invested at this lone city, not 'guarding' it. Idiomatic 'besieging' is right; literal 'guarding' reverses the military stance.

proposals.before: Enraged, Hao marched north on news from Guanzhong; Xiang sprang the trap at Shansang, cut him to pieces, stacked ten thousand heads, and captured wagons and weapons.
proposals.after: Enraged, Hao marched north on news from Guanzhong; Xiang sprang the trap at Shansang, cut him to pieces, killed and captured by the myriad, and seized wagons and weapons.
proposals.reason: 斬獲萬計 is killed-and-captured by the myriad, not specifically stacked heads. Mild overstatement; literal is accurate.

proposals.before: Yao Chang, courtesy Maomao, ranked twenty-fourth among Yizhong's sons.
proposals.after: Yao Chang, courtesy Jingmao, ranked twenty-fourth among Yizhong's sons.
proposals.reason: Courtesy name 景茂 is Jingmao; both English fields invent Maomao. Cross-chapter Jinshu 119 correctly uses Jingmao; extraction p031 courtesy alias also stores Maomao.

proposals.before: Chang's courtesy name was Maomao; he was Yizhong's twenty-fourth son.
proposals.after: Chang's courtesy name was Jingmao; he was Yizhong's twenty-fourth son.
proposals.reason: Courtesy name 景茂 is Jingmao; current literal Maomao is a definite mistransliteration (same error as idiomatic / extraction alias).

proposals.before: When Liang later bolted to Huan Wen, Wen asked his verdict: "He has Sun Ce's magnetism and stature—only his battlefield edge is greater."
proposals.after: When Liang later bolted to Huan Wen, Wen asked Liang about Xiang; Liang said: "He has Sun Ce's divine bearing and breadth of mind—only his battlefield prowess is greater."
proposals.reason: Chinese 溫問襄於亮 makes Xiang the asked-about referent; idiomatic 'Wen asked his verdict' drops that proposition. Quote also compresses 神明器宇…雄武過之, but the missing 'about Xiang' is the clear coverage gap.

proposals.before: He climbed through left guard general, a chain of western prefectures—Longdong, Ji, Hedong, Wudu, Weiba, Brazil, Fufeng—three provincial inspectorships, a second tour as general who spreads might, colonel of foot, and the marquisate of Yidu.
proposals.after: He climbed through left guard general; prefect of Longdong, Ji, Hedong, Wudu, Wuwei, Baxi, and Fufeng; inspector of Ning, You, and Yan; a second tour as general who spreads might; colonel of foot; and the marquisate of Yidu.
proposals.reason: 武威 is Wuwei, not Weiba; corpus convention for 巴西 is Baxi (not Brazil). Idiomatic also drops the named inspectorships 甯、幽、兗.

proposals.before: He successively served as general of the Left Guard, prefect of Longdong, Ji, Hedong, Wudu, Weiba, Brazil, and Fufeng, inspector of Ning, You, and Yan, again General Who Spreads Might, colonel of infantry, and was enfeoffed Marquis of Yidu.
proposals.after: He successively served as general of the Left Guard, prefect of Longdong, Ji, Hedong, Wudu, Wuwei, Baxi, and Fufeng, inspector of Ning, You, and Yan, again General Who Spreads Might, colonel of infantry, and was enfeoffed Marquis of Yidu.
proposals.reason: 武威 mistranslated Weiba; 巴西 should be Baxi per chapter corpus convention (e.g. jinshu 004/082/125).

proposals.before: Chong's general Gao Gai marched fifty thousand south of Xinping and collapsed; Gai brought thousands over and won a supernumerary attendant's tile.
proposals.after: Chong's chariot-and-horse grand general Gao Gai marched fifty thousand; south of Xinping Chang shattered him; Gai brought thousands over and won a supernumerary attendant's tile.

proposals.after: At Qinzhou he faced Wang Tong until droves—Tuge in Tianshui, Qiang and Hu in Lüeyang—swelled his rolls; Tong yielded.

proposals.before: He then went to Qinzhou and locked horns with Wang Tong, Jian's inspector of Qinzhou; two-plus ten thousand households of Tujue Luochuan in Tianshui and Qiang Hu of Lüeyang answered Chang; Tong feared and surrendered.

proposals.before: Lan Niu of Fengyi broke with Fu Shinu under Murong Yong's hammer and cried for aid.
proposals.after: Lan Du of Fengyi broke with Fu Shinu; Murong Yong attacked him, and Du cried for aid.
proposals.reason: 蘭犢 is Lan Du (犢 dú); 'Lan Niu' is a definite mistransliteration (jinshu 115 correctly uses Lan Du; extraction p124 English Lan Niu contradicts its own pinyin Lán Dú). Also idiomatic fuses 與苻師奴離貳，慕容永攻之 so that Murong Yong appears to cause the split.

proposals.before: Deng's prefect of Fengyi Lan Niu split from Fu Shinu; Murong Yong attacked him; Niu sent envoys begging rescue.
proposals.after: Deng's prefect of Fengyi Lan Du split from Fu Shinu; Murong Yong attacked him; Du sent envoys begging rescue.
proposals.reason: 蘭犢 mistranslated Lan Niu; must be Lan Du.

proposals.before: Lan Niu fell too, men and mounts included.
proposals.after: Lan Du fell too, men and mounts included.
proposals.reason: Continues Lan Niu error for 蘭犢; should be Lan Du.

proposals.before: He also seized Lan Niu and gathered his soldiers and horses.
proposals.after: He also seized Lan Du and gathered his soldiers and horses.

proposals.before: Years of stalemate and Deng's victories sapped loyalty—yet Qi Nan, Xu Luosheng, Liu Guodan, Mizijie Poluo, Zhao Edi, Liang Guoer and a handful kept the pledge, sons guarding baggage trains while fathers rode with Chang.
proposals.after: Years of stalemate and Deng's victories sapped loyalty—yet Qi Nan, Xu Luosheng, Liu Guodan, Mizijie Pochu, Zhao Edi, Liang Guoer and a handful kept the pledge, sons guarding baggage trains while fathers rode with Chang.
proposals.reason: 彌姐婆觸 given name 婆觸 is Pochu (觸 chù); Poluo is wrong. Extraction p133 English Mizijie Poluo contradicts its pinyin Póchù.

proposals.before: After Chang locked horns with Fu Deng year on year and repeatedly suffered Deng's defeats, near and far alike harbored plans to leave or join; only General Who Conquers Captives Qi Nan, Champion Xu Luosheng, Assistant to the State Liu Guodan, Champion Might Mizijie Poluo, Dragon-General Zhao Edi, General Who Guards the North Liang Guoer and others kept faith undivided, all leaving sons to guard camps, supplying successive army grain, themselves leading picked troops to follow Chang on campaign.
proposals.after: After Chang locked horns with Fu Deng year on year and repeatedly suffered Deng's defeats, near and far alike harbored plans to leave or join; only General Who Conquers Captives Qi Nan, Champion Xu Luosheng, Assistant to the State Liu Guodan, Champion Might Mizijie Pochu, Dragon-General Zhao Edi, General Who Guards the North Liang Guoer and others kept faith undivided, all leaving sons to guard camps, supplying successive army grain, themselves leading picked troops to follow Chang on campaign.

proposals.before: Suo Luyao of Dunhuang volunteered to murder Fu Deng; Chang asked, "You stake your life—for whom?"
proposals.after: Suolu Yao of Dunhuang volunteered to murder Fu Deng; Chang asked, "You stake your life—for whom?"
proposals.reason: 索盧曜 is compound surname 索盧 + given name 曜 (Suolu Yao), not Suo + Luyao. Parallel tribal/name treatment uses Suolu elsewhere (e.g. jinshu 125).

proposals.before: Suo Luyao of Dunhuang asked to assassinate Fu Deng; Chang said: "You offer your body for peril—on whose behalf?"
proposals.after: Suolu Yao of Dunhuang asked to assassinate Fu Deng; Chang said: "You offer your body for peril—on whose behalf?"
proposals.reason: 索盧曜 mis-segmented as Suo Luyao; should be Suolu Yao.

proposals.before: Luyao said: "After my death I deeply entrust my friend Xin Xian of Longxi to your care."
proposals.after: Yao said: "After my death I deeply entrust my friend Xin Xian of Longxi to your care."
proposals.reason: Literal 'Luyao said' continues Suo Luyao mis-segmentation; subject is Yao.

proposals.before: Fu Deng borrows a flock of crow-struck dogs and sheep, stealing breath to survive; gauge his wit and courage—he is no peer for Your Majesty.
proposals.after: Fu Deng borrows a ragtag flock of dogs and sheep, stealing breath to survive; gauge his wit and courage—he is no peer for Your Majesty.
proposals.reason: 烏合 means a ragtag/hastily assembled host, not 'crow-struck'. Literal invents an etymology from 烏; idiomatic 'mongrel host' already covers the proposition.

proposals.before: Wei Hefei proclaimed himself grand general and Heaven-Rushing King, threw Di and Hu tens of thousands deep against Yao Dangcheng at Xingcheng; Lei Edi pitched in against Yao Hande at Lirun.
proposals.after: Wei Hefei proclaimed himself grand general and Heaven-Rushing King, threw Di and Hu tens of thousands deep against General Who Guards the North Yao Dangcheng at Xingcheng; Lei Edi pitched in against General Who Guards the East Yao Hande at Lirun.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic drops office titles 安北 and 鎮東 that name Yao Dangcheng and Yao Hande; literal retains both.

proposals.before: Ministers protested, "Fu Deng sits sixty li off while Hefei marches six hundred—why fear the distant bandit?"
proposals.after: Chang debated campaigning against them; ministers protested, "Fu Deng sits sixty li off while Hefei marches six hundred—why fear the distant bandit?"
proposals.reason: Idiomatic omits 萇議將討之 (Chang debated campaigning); the Chinese opens with Chang's deliberation before the ministers speak. Literal is complete.

proposals.before: He explained, "They flock together—one whirlwind sweep empties their nests."
proposals.after: His staff wondered and asked; Chang explained, "Now men of shared wickedness aid each other and all flock here—I can ride victory, roll them up, and empty their nests in one blow; nothing will remain in the northeast."
proposals.reason: Idiomatic collapses Chang's reply and drops 群下怪而問之, 同惡相濟，皆來會集, and 東北無復餘也. Literal preserves the propositions.

proposals.before: Chang hugged his walls, feigned frailty, then slipped Chong around with hundreds of riders.
proposals.after: Chang hugged his walls, feigned frailty, then secretly sent his son Chong around with hundreds of riders.
